title: Second Punic War (218–201 BCE)
key_facts: Hannibal’s campaign against Rome, including the crossing of the Alps
Major Carthaginian victories at Trebia, Lake Trasimene, and Cannae
Roman recovery under Scipio Africanus culminating in victory at Zama (202 BCE)
causes: Renewed rivalry after the First Punic War and disputes in Iberia
Saguntum affair triggered hostilities between Rome and Carthage
outcome: Carthage lost overseas territories and naval power; heavy indemnities
Rome asserted dominance across the western Mediterranean
impacts: Demonstrated Roman resilience and adaptive strategy
Shifted balance decisively toward Roman hegemony
